key_insight: AlgoRAG shows that a retrieval-augmented LLM can deliver correct, pedagogically useful explanations for highly abstract theoretical computer science topics by combining curated sources with notation-aware retrieval.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests RAG is a practical architecture for building domain-specific tutoring systems in computational science, especially where formal proofs and algorithm analysis require adaptive, context-rich guidance.
method: Curated knowledge base: textbooks, lecture slides, practice problems, proof templates, and worksheets.
Domain-specific retrieval: mathematical entity recognition, notation-aware matching, and pedagogical re-ranking.
Evaluation on exam-style TCS questions across asymptotic analysis, DP, graphs, NP-completeness, sorting, and divide-and-conquer.
evidence_signal: The system was evaluated on 179 curated questions and achieved 100% success with mean response time of 38.0 seconds, alongside ROUGE-1 F1 of 0.0963 and pedagogical quality of 0.7620.
watch_item: BLEU-4 is zero and the reported metrics rely on surface overlap, so the main concern is that n-gram scores may understate correct but differently phrased mathematical reasoning and the system’s robustness depends on high-quality curated retrieval sources.
paper_title: AlgoRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Theoretical Computer Science Education -- A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for Algorithm Analysis and Complexity Theory
